title: Coherence of Hom transport with the original counits
statement: Assume shared derived-category instances for the module category of every scheme [def-pc-derived-category]. For a scheme morphism $s:X\to S$, put $p_T:X\times_S T\to X$ for the projection associated to an object $T\to S$ of $\mathrm{Over}(S)$. For an arrow $g:T'\to T$ over $S$ and $P,Q\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, use equality $p_T\circ\operatorname{baseChangeMap}(s,g)=p_{T'}$ and the inverse original-counit composition lift [lem-pc-recorded-pullback-composition] to define $C_g:Lp_{T'}^*\cong Lg_X^*\circ Lp_T^*$, where $g_X=\operatorname{baseChangeMap}(s,g)$ and derived pullback is [def-pc-derived-pullback]. Define $M_g(a)=C_g(P)\,Lg_X^*(a)\,C_g(Q)^{-1}$ for $a:Lp_T^*P\to Lp_T^*Q$. These maps preserve identity and composition; $M_g(a)=M_g(b)$ if and only if $Lg_X^*(a)=Lg_X^*(b)$; and $M_h(M_g(a))=M_{g\circ h}(a)$ for every $h:T''\to T'$ over $S$. In particular, let $I$ be preordered, $R:I\to\mathrm{CommRing}$ a diagram and $c$ a cocone with vertex $A$. For $i\leq j\leq k$ and $s:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(R_i)$, the induced maps from $j$ to $k$ and from stages to $A$ satisfy $M_{kA}(M_{jk}(a))=M_{jA}(a)$ for every morphism between the stage-$j$ pullbacks of $P,Q$. No colimit, directedness, perfectness or finite-presentation assumption is needed for this identity.

proof.text: Evaluate associativity on P and Q. Naturality at the transported morphism and cancellation of comparison inverses yield composition of conjugated Hom maps. Equality transport handles baseChangeMap_fst, and baseChangeMap_comp identifies successive base-change arrows. Functor map laws prove identity/composition and invertible conjugation proves equality detection. The private recordedTr and recordedTrTo constructions explicitly use recordedPerfectHomComposition; their associativity and equality-transport lemmas concern these original-counit lifts, not the old chosen perfectHomComposition. Distinct helper names and explicit derived-category binders keep the two constructions unambiguous.
